description: Polyphonic meta modulator: it cross-modulates two signals through nine algorithms, from crossfading and wavefolding to ring modulation and a vocoder, with a frequency shifter alongside them

params.text: Blends between the nine cross-modulation algorithms in turn; with F.S on it sets the amount of frequency shift, or the amount of phase shift in quadrature mode
Sets the shaping parameter of the algorithm in use; with F.S on it balances the lower and upper sidebands, both of them present at the centre
Cycles the internal oscillator through off and three waveforms, which feed the first module channel in place of input 1; with F.S on it chooses the quadrature modulator or one of three shifter waves
Sets the level of the signal at input 1; with the internal oscillator on it sets that oscillator's frequency instead, and with F.S on the amount of feedback
Sets the level of the signal at input 2; a control voltage can push this gain past unity, which gives a warm overdrive
Switches the module from the cross-modulation algorithms to the frequency shifter and the quadrature cross-modulator

inputs.text: Scales the first level knob, 5V giving the knob's own setting; with the internal oscillator on it sets that oscillator's pitch at one volt per octave. With nothing patched it reads 5V
Scales the second level knob, 5V giving the knob's own setting and more than that overdriving it; with nothing patched it reads 5V
Shifts the algorithm away from the one the big knob picks, 5V covering the whole sweep, and each polyphonic channel takes its own offset
Adds to the TIMBRE knob, 5V covering the whole knob range
The carrier signal, which most of the algorithms filter or modulate so that it takes on the character of the other input; its channel count helps set the module's polyphony
The modulator signal, which most of the algorithms impose on the carrier; its channel count helps set the module's polyphony

outputs.text: The main output, ±5V; with F.S on it carries one of the two sidebands, or the real part of the result in quadrature mode
The two inputs summed after their level controls, or the bare internal oscillator while that is on; with F.S on it carries the other sideband, or the imaginary part in quadrature mode

notes: the module is polyphonic: the channel count comes from whichever of the two audio inputs carries more, and every channel runs its own copy of the modulator.
the two module channels are not the polyphonic channels: each polyphonic channel has a channel 1 and a channel 2 of its own, fed by the two audio inputs or by the internal oscillator.
the two level jacks read 5V when nothing is patched, which is full gain, so each level knob works on its own.
bypassing the module passes input 2 straight to the main output.

inputs.0:
0 to 5V · continuous · polyphonic

unpatched it reads 5V, or 2V for the oscillator pitch; a negative voltage does nothing here.
inputs.1:
0 to 5V · continuous · polyphonic

unpatched it reads 5V; a negative voltage does nothing here.
inputs.2:
continuous · polyphonic

a negative voltage subtracts from the knob; the knob and this input are summed and the total held to 0 to 5V.
inputs.3:
continuous · polyphonic

a negative voltage subtracts from the knob; the knob and this input are summed and the total held to 0 to 5V.
